newsitem.title: UK: Ukraine plans move towards currency convertibility.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine plans move towards currency convertibility.

text.p: Ukraine plans to take a step towards making its hryvnia currency convertible by adhering to Article 8 of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) after the 1997 budget is approved, Finance Minister Ihor Mityukov said.

Mityukov told Reuters at this weekend's meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) that the government would introduce a package of measures to parliament that would remove remaining obstacles to joining Article 8.
"Immediately after the budget is adopted, the government and the National Bank will take the necessary steps for Ukraine to finally adhere to Article 8 of the IMF," he said.
The move, already undertaken by Russia, effectively means that Ukraine would promise not to restrict payments and transfers for foreign trade operations.
The hryvnia, like the Russian rouble, cannot be freely traded outside of the borders of the respective countries.
Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma last month called for adoption of a currency corridor or trading band for the hryvnia as a way of boosting the former Soviet republic's export potential.
He also said Ukraine needed to seek full convertibility for the currency in line with Article 8.

But reforms were dealt a blow earlier this month when deputy prime minister Viktor Pynzenyk resigned, accusing parliament and the government of dragging their heels on approving the budget and tax changes.
The budget, which could pave the way for Ukraine to receive a $2.5 to $3 billion loan from the IMF, had been due for parliamentary approval on January 1.
Mityukov said he would like to see a currency corridor established with permitted fluctuations of no more than 10 percent. "I would prefer to have five."
"I think this year we could agree with the central bank about changing the basics in currency policy.
